images.filename: Afghanistan Camp Russell Memorial, Australian War Memorial.jpg
images.caption:
Afghanistan Camp Russell Memorial, Australian War MemorialThe sign reads: Memorial from Camp Russell Uruzgan province, Afghanistan
Australians first deployed to Afghanistan in 2001. From 2005 to 2013, most Australian personnel were stationed at Tarin Kot in Uruzgan province.
The Australian Special Forces and supporting units were based in Camp Russell. The camp was named after the first Australian to be killed in Afghanistan Sergeant Andrew Russell of the Special Air Service Regiment.
Although located within the confines of a larger coalition base (Camp Holland), Camp Russell was a secure and separate enclosure which contained living, medical, and operational facilities. This memorial was the focus for various commemorative ceremonies, such as Anzac Day and Remembrance Day, but was also used during special services held to farewell comrades killed in action.
The memorial used for commemorations in Camp Holland - previously displayed on the plinth adjacent to this one - was removed from display in 2020 following damage caused by exposure to weather.
REL48377
A member of the Special Operations Engineer Regiment pays tribute on Anzac Day, 25 April 2012.

IMAGE COURTESY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENCE

Dusk at the Australian War Memorial in Canberra. During dry times kangaroos make their way in from the surrounding bushland to feed on the well-watered green lawns of the Memorial. Here a couple pose before a 5-inch gun turret from now scrapped HMAS Brisbane, which saw service in Vietnam.

See also File:HMAS Brisbane AWM Nov 08.JPG for same view in November 2008 after addition of HMAS Brisbane's bridge.
